lines: Easy bruising and frequent nosebleeds for the past 18 months.

Her current medications include prednisone 10 mg daily.

encounters.cc: Worsening bruising, new episodes of epistaxis, and increasing gum bleeding 10 days after initial ITP diagnosis.

lines: Worsening bruising, new episodes of epistaxis, and increasing gum bleeding 10 days after initial ITP diagnosis.
The patient is a 42-year-old female with immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) who returns to the clinic for follow-up evaluation approximately 10 days following her initial diagnosis.
She initially presented with spontaneous bruising and bleeding gums, and laboratory evaluation at that time demonstrated isolated thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 11,000/mm³.
Peripheral smear was normal aside from large platelets, and prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) were within normal limits.
She was started on oral prednisone at the prior visit.
She currently denies hematuria, melena, or changes in neurologic status, and reports no history of trauma.
The patient has been adherent to prednisone and reports no side effects.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily
- No family history of bleeding disorders
Examination reveals multiple new petechiae on the lower extremities and ecchymoses on the forearms and thighs.
There is dried blood at the gumline but no active bleeding.
No hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy is noted.
Repeat labs show a hemoglobin level of 12.3 g/dL, leukocyte count of 6,900/mm³, and platelet count of 9,000/mm³.

lines: Increased bruising over the past two weeks with occasional nosebleeds.
The patient returns for follow-up of chronic ITP diagnosed January 2020.
She reports noticing easy bruising on her arms and legs without significant trauma.
She also has occasional nosebleeds that are difficult to stop.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily
- No family history of bleeding disorders
Physical examination reveals multiple petechiae and ecchymoses on the extremities.
There is no hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy.

encounters.cc: Easy bruising and increased bleeding from gums over the past 5 days, with prolonged nosebleed lasting 30 minutes.

lines: Easy bruising and increased bleeding from gums over the past 5 days, with prolonged nosebleed lasting 30 minutes.
The patient is a 43-year-old female with a known history of chronic immune thrombocytopenic purpura diagnosed in January 2020 who returns to the emergency department with recurrent bleeding symptoms.
She presents approximately six months following her last outpatient hematology evaluation with similar complaints.
She says she first noticed purplish discoloration on her thighs and upper arms that appeared spontaneously.
Over the past two days, she has experienced bleeding after brushing her teeth and a prolonged nosebleed lasting nearly 30 minutes.
She denies hematuria, melena, or heavy menstrual bleeding.
She has not had recent dental work or trauma.
She recalls having a mild upper respiratory infection about two weeks ago, which resolved without treatment.
She has no personal or family history of bleeding disorders.
She is not taking any anticoagulants or NSAIDs.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily
She has no personal or family history of bleeding disorders
On exam, her vital signs are normal.
She appears well and in no distress.
There are several ecchymoses over her arms and thighs, and petechiae are noted on both lower extremities.
Her gums are mildly erythematous with residual dried blood, but there is no active bleeding.
There is no hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy.
Neurologic and cardiopulmonary exams are normal.
Laboratory testing reveals a hemoglobin level of 12.9 g/dL, leukocyte count of 6,700/mm³, and platelet count of 14,000/mm³.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset weakness of the right side of her face following recent upper respiratory illness.

lines: Sudden-onset weakness of the right side of her face following recent upper respiratory illness.
This 44-year-old female with chronic ITP and recurrent bleeding complications presents to Neurology.
She is unable to close her right eye, raise her right eyebrow, or smile symmetrically.
She reports recent recovery from an upper respiratory illness.
She denies rash, ear pain, and tick exposure.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily
- No family history of bleeding disorders
Neurologic examination reveals complete right-sided facial paralysis.
Strength and sensation in the limbs are normal.

encounters.cc: 2-day history of severe vertigo, nausea, and vomiting preventing daily activities.

lines: 2-day history of severe vertigo, nausea, and vomiting preventing daily activities.

This 45-year-old female with chronic immune thrombocytopenic purpura maintained on prednisone and history of Bell's palsy reports that symptoms started suddenly and have persisted, preventing her from performing daily activities.
She also notes a recent upper respiratory tract infection that resolved a week ago.
The patient denies any hearing loss or tinnitus.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily
- No family history of bleeding disorders
Vital signs are within normal limits
On examination, she has spontaneous nystagmus that increases when she looks to the left and a positive Romberg sign.
She is unable to perform the Dix-Hallpike maneuver due to severe nausea.
